CanonicalVars.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 24.) All 23 cards now store their printed C# var under a `_`-attribute (or, for 3 cards whose C# var is a live/computed value at display time -- guilty, normality, expect_a_fight -- a `magic_number` property override; wither similarly overrides `base_damage`) so `Card.base_damage`/`base_block`/`base_hp_loss`/`magic_number` report the C# value instead of the 0/None default. Two additive base.py changes: `_frail` added to `_MAGIC_ATTRS` (shame) and a new `base_gold` property (debt, spoils_map -- GoldVar had no base property at all). feel_no_pain's `_block` was renamed to `_power_amount` (fixing a WRONG value, not just a missing one -- `base_block` no longer misreports it as block-granting; matches Rage/Corruption/Stampede's DynamicVar('Power', ...) convention). Combat behavior / dealt numbers are byte-identical in every case -- a printed-number / observation-encoder fix only. 3 of the 23 (debt, spoils_map, rolling_boulder's secondary IncrementAmount) have NO obs-vector change despite the API fix (full_env.py has no base_gold read site; magic_number carries one number per card and _power_amount dominates rolling_boulder's scan) -- documented, not closed further. CHECKPOINT NOTE for training: encoded VALUES changed for the other 20 cards in feature slots f[17]/f[18] damage, f[20]/f[21] block, f[22] hp_loss, f[23] magic_number; obs LAYOUT unchanged. Pins: test/test_printed_vars.py (48 tests).  The text it replaced read: `new DamageVar(17m, ValueProp.Move)` maps to `_damage = 17`, and the second var `new CardsVar(3)` (PactsEnd.cs:15-19) IS stored -- but under the name `_required_exhausted`, which is not in `Card._MAGIC_ATTRS` (cards/base.py:185-189), so `magic_number` returns None where the game prints 3. The VALUE is right and the behaviour is right; only the printed-number API misses it, which for this card is the number that decides whether the play does anything at all. A one-word rename to `_cards` would surface it. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's `magic_number` cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.maps_to: PactsEndCard.on_play, routed per-enemy by the framework (pacts_end.py:37-41; combat.py:1164-1174)
OnPlay.issue: Re-audited 2026-08-04 (stale-sweep task-8 batch-04): still open, citations refreshed only, content re-confirmed unchanged. The gate and the damage are faithful: `CanDealDamage` is `CardPile.GetCards(Owner, PileType.Exhaust).Count() >= Cards.IntValue` (PactsEnd.cs:23) == `if len(ctx.player.exhaust_pile) < self._cards: return` (renamed from `_required_exhausted`), and the whole play is a no-op below the threshold on both sides. Leaving `handles_own_routing` False is correct for a one-hit AoE (combat.py:1164, `if card.target_type == TargetType.ALL_ENEMIES and not card.handles_own_routing`). One nuance recorded rather than verdicted: because the framework calls `on_play` once per living enemy, the sim re-evaluates the exhaust-pile gate PER ENEMY where C# evaluates it once -- harmless, since nothing in the attack changes the exhaust pile, but it would matter for a gate that the attack itself could flip. ALL-ENEMIES FAN-OUT: C# passes the whole valid-target list to ONE `CreatureCmd.Damage(targets: validTargets)` call (AttackCommand.cs:650), computing every DamageResult before any `Kill` (CreatureCmd.cs:372-409); the sim issues a separate `DamageCmd.deal` per enemy, so each death resolves before the next enemy is damaged. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/conflagration's OnPlay entry (rule 3). DORMANT (both RL-training and conformance-replay) -- no ported Ironclad-reachable monster has an on-death effect that changes a sibling's incoming damage.
